jobs.description:
Overview

Organization Summary

At Global Vendor Delivery & Solutions (GVDS), we are transforming how Microsoft delivers business operations at scale. As part of MBO (Microsoft Business Operations), GVDS combines operational excellence, AI-powered innovation, and strategic partnerships to create secure, scalable, and high-performing services across a global vendor ecosystem.

As Microsoft evolves toward a Frontier Firm model, AI, automation, and agentic systems are reshaping how work gets done. GVDS plays a critical role in enabling that transformation by helping operations become more intelligent, adaptive, and outcome-focused. We are looking for leaders who can challenge legacy approaches, accelerate adoption of AI-first ways of working, and build sustainable systems that continuously improve customer and business outcomes.

Role Summary

The AI Transformation & Continuous Improvement Lead is responsible for embedding a culture of continuous improvement across Vendor Operations while accelerating the adoption of AI-enabled operating models. This role serves as a strategic bridge between operations, engineering, service design, and vendor partners to identify opportunities for transformation, eliminate inefficiencies, and drive measurable business outcomes.

Success in this role requires equal parts transformational leadership, operational excellence, and change management. The ideal candidate will build scalable improvement systems, champion AI-driven innovation, and advance Vendor Operations toward a Frontier Firm model that delivers greater quality, productivity, customer satisfaction, and business value.

This is not a traditional Continuous Improvement role focused solely on Lean methodologies. It is a transformation leadership role responsible for helping redefine how operations are designed, executed, measured, and continuously optimized in an AI-first world.

Responsibilities

Capability Portfolio Ownership & Feature Management

Own the strategy, roadmap, prioritization, business cases, implementation governance, adoption, benefits realization, and continuous improvement of a portfolio of artificial intelligence-driven operational capabilities.
Maintain accountability beyond deployment to ensure capabilities continue to evolve and deliver measurable business outcomes.

AI Transformation & Frontier Firm Enablement

Lead the adoption of AI-first and agentic operating models across Vendor Operations.
Identify opportunities to automate manual processes and improve decision-making through AI-enabled workflows.
Partner with engineering, service design, and operations teams to scale AI and automation capabilities.
Drive operational readiness for Microsoft's Frontier Firm vision.

Continuous Improvement System Deployment

Establish and scale continuous improvement practices across Vendor Operations using Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA), Lean, or other structured problem-solving methodologies.
Build repeatable improvement frameworks that create sustainable operational gains.
Facilitate cross-functional improvement initiatives that drive measurable business impact.
Ensure improvements are standardized and institutionalized through governance and operational rhythms.

Operational Excellence & Performance Management

Define and track metrics that reflect customer value, operational efficiency, quality, productivity, and adoption of AI-enabled capabilities.
Develop performance insights that enable leaders to prioritize investments and improvement opportunities.
Create visibility into operational health and transformation progress through data-driven reporting.

Change Management & Organizational Adoption

Lead adoption strategies for new capabilities, operating models, tools, and ways of working, using stakeholder feedback and performance data to guide ongoing capability improvements.
Partner with stakeholders to remove barriers and accelerate behavioral change.
Ensure improvements transition from pilots to sustainable business practices.
Build organizational capability for continuous learning and improvement.

Cross-Functional Leadership & Influence

Serve as a trusted advisor to Vendor Operations leaders on transformation priorities and continuous improvement strategy.
Align stakeholders across Vendor Operations, Engineering, Service Design, and broader MBO initiatives.
Foster knowledge sharing and reuse of best practices across the vendor ecosystem.
Drive organizational alignment around operational excellence and business outcomes.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's Degree in Business, Operations, Finance, or related field AND 4+ years experience in program management, process management, or process improvement OR equivalent experience.

Preferred Qualifications

6+ years of experience leading operational transformation, continuous improvement, or business process optimization initiatives in complex global organizations.
Demonstrated success driving measurable improvements in quality, productivity, customer experience, or operational efficiency.
Strong data-driven decision-making skills with experience defining and managing operational performance metrics.
Proven ability to influence organizational boundaries and lead without direct authority. Strong executive communication, stakeholder management, and leadership skills.
Experience owning a portfolio of operational capabilities or features, including strategy, roadmap planning, prioritization, business case development, implementation governance, adoption, and benefits realization.
Experience deploying AI, automation, or agentic solutions within operational environments.
Experience implementing structured improvement methodologies such as Lean, PDCA, Kaizen, or related frameworks.
Knowledge of vendor operations, outsourcing models, or large-scale service delivery organizations.
Experience partnering with engineering, product, or service design teams on transformation initiatives.
Familiarity with Responsible AI principles and AI governance considerations.
Certification or experience in Lean Six Sigma or comparable continuous improvement disciplines.

Success Measures

Success In This Role Will Be Measured By

Adoption and scalability of continuous improvement practices across Vendor Operations.
Increased AI-enabled automation and reduction of manual effort.
Improvements in customer satisfaction, quality, productivity, and operational efficiency.
Demonstrated business impact from transformation initiatives.
Increased organizational capability and adoption of AI-first ways of working.
Establishment of sustainable operational excellence and governance practices.
Contribution toward the evolution of Vendor Operations into a Frontier Firm operating model.

new_jobs.title: Care Manager II
new_jobs.description:
IOA is on the forefront of revolutionary healthcare models, reshaping the way people can age in place. Our innovative models transform lives, enhance communities, and save healthcare systems millions of dollars. Rather than focusing on archaic outdated design, we strive to consistently question the “status-quo” and create new and more innovative ways to help aging adults and adults with disabilities maintain their quality of life.

With over 23 programs, we offer multiple ways to aid seniors maintain their health, well-being, independence and participation in the community, fulfilling our mission.

IOA's Care Manager II (CMII) is responsible for the assessment of clients with multiple medical and psychosocial needs. The CMII also plans for and monitors services and interventions ensuring provision of quality care.

Responsibilities

Conducts comprehensive assessments and on-going re-assessments of the client including psychosocial, physical and mental health, environmental and spiritual needs.
Writes comprehensive assessments. Based on assessment information with the client develops and initiates the Community Living Plan, which is client-centered, comprehensive and consistent with program guidelines and policies and procedures.
Conducts home visits, acute hospital & skilled nursing facility visits, as well as escorts clients to medical and other appointments as clinically indicated.
Identifies, arranges for, and monitors appropriate community services based on a good knowledge of Medicare, Medi-Cal, and other entitlement programs.
Establishes and maintains a care management relationship with clients and their informal support network as appropriate, offering respect, dignity and support. Provides crisis intervention, advocacy, problem solving and therapeutic interventions.
Meets with clients at least monthly, and more often as clinically indicated. Reviews and modifies their Community Living Plan on an ongoing basis.
Documents via progress notes all case management activity regarding identified problems within 24-48 hours, adding any new problems to the Community Living Plan, as needed.
Maintains required paperwork and follows a clear, concise, and consistent system of charting to allow for continuity of care.
Ongoing evaluation for client Purchase of Service needs and follow-up to determine if services have been provided in a timely manner.
Educates clients and informal support network about resources.
Establishes and maintains open and effective communication with community providers, including physicians and other health care and social service workers. Provides appropriate information on all significant aspects of individual client care and program operations, while maintaining necessary confidentiality.
Monitors the quantity and quality of the services provided by other involved providers.
Working closely with the team, continuously evaluates the clients’ ability to remain safely at home, coordinates placement as appropriate, according to program guidelines.
In collaboration with the client, caregiver, and involved services, terminates clients when appropriate. Documents the process as required.
Participates in research studies and data collection, as required.
Participates in and promotes ongoing efforts towards Continuous Quality Improvement.
Attends and actively participates in team and program meetings, activities and problem-solving endeavors; contributes to open lines of communication within the team.
Utilizes supervision appropriately, maintaining open lines of communication and providing updates on caseload activity.
Actively incorporates the ethical and legal standards of the National Association of Social Workers into all aspects of interactions with others.
Understands and applies the regulatory and procedural requirements of the Institute on Aging.
Attends continuing education classes and/or in-service training to increase knowledge, skills and attitudes related to case management, gerontology, family and community systems and other areas relevant to the Community Living Fund client population.
All other reasonably related responsibilities as assigned.

Education

M.S.W. (Masters in Social Work) or another appropriate Masters level degree such as an MPH, MFT with additional or specialized work experience such as psychology, counseling, or geriatrics.
Alternatively, in lieu of a Masters degree, an employee may qualify for a Care Manager II position with a BA or BS in Social Work or another appropriate major and a minimum of two (2) years of relevant social work experience and the ability to demonstrate autonomous work in conceptualizing and formulating biopsychosocial assessments, identifying care needs and necessary interventions, and then executing effective care interventions.

Background And Experience

One year working with disabled adults and/or older adults required.
Experience with and understanding of the medical and psychosocial problems of functionally impaired adults and older adults.
Experience working with individuals with mental and/or behavioral health diagnoses and substance abuse disorders highly desired.
Exceptional communication and presentation skills relating to functionally impaired adults and older adults, their support systems and teams of health professionals.
Demonstrates case management skills and experience in the community health care delivery system.
Detail oriented with good problem solving skills and the ability to prioritize multiple tasks.
Computer literacy required.
EPIC electronic medical records experience highly preferred.

Company Description

At Lucile Packard Children’s Hospital Stanford, we know world-renowned care begins with world-class caring. That's why we combine advanced technologies and breakthrough discoveries with family-centered care. It's why we provide our caregivers with continuing education and state-of-the-art facilities, like the newly remodeled Lucile Packard Children's Hospital Stanford. And it's why we need caring, committed people on our team - like you. Join us on our mission to heal humanity, one child and family at a time.

Job ID:
LP_00026205-2658560

Job Description

JOB SUMMARY

This paragraph summarizes the general nature, level and purpose of the job.

The Assistant Patient Care Manager is responsible for assisting the Patient Care Manager with clinical management and administrative coordination of a designated patient care unit(s) or service(s). The position supports the Patient Care Manager in promoting the achievement of the unit(s)' goals and objectives. This position works in a supportive manner as a resource for the patient care unit(s) and as a representative for the Patient Care Manager. Typically assigned responsibility for supervising patient care staff and operations for an assigned shift for a patient care unit(s) and/or for coordinating one or more administrative functions as assigned by the Patient Care Manager, ensuring consistent implementation and monitoring of organizational policies and standards of care, their work involves a combination of clinical (patient care) and administrative responsibilities. The Assistant Patient Care Manager provides consistent and timely information and feedback to the Patient Care Manager and is responsible for knowledge and application of all personnel policies and requirements of the collective bargaining agreements. Assistant Patient Care Managers differ from Patient Care Managers in that the latter are unit managers with total responsibility and accountability for one or more patient care units or services.

Essential Functions

The essential functions listed are typical examples of work performed by positions in this job classification. They are not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, tasks, and responsibilities. Employees may also perform other duties as assigned.

Employees must abide by all Joint Commission Requirements including but not limited to sensitivity to cultural diversity, patient care, patient rights and ethical treatment, safety and security of physical environments, emergency management, teamwork, respect for others, participation in ongoing education and training, communication and adherence to safety and quality programs, sustaining compliance with National Patient Safety Goals, and licensure and health screenings.

Must perform all duties and responsibilities in accordance with the hospital's policies and procedures, including its Service Standards and its Code of Conduct.

Assists in the performance of the operational aspects of a designated unit(s) while providing mentoring and leadership support to the unit(s) staff; supervises the provision of quality, therapeutic and cost-effective patient care in accordance with standards of practice, hospital protocols, policies and procedures, and desired patient outcomes.
Assists Patient Care Manager in administrative/management functions and assumes the duties and responsibilities of the Patient Care Manager as delegated and/or in the case of absence.
Coordinates and directs the unit(s) patient care operations for an assigned shift, acting on behalf of the Patient Care Manager.
Facilitates orientation, training and ongoing staff development; assists in coaching, developing and corrective action of personnel as appropriate; participates in ongoing and annual evaluation of employee performance.
Facilitates the effective delivery of competent, compassionate care by monitoring and evaluating patient care processes and outcomes to facilitate smooth workflow and desired outcomes on the patient care unit(s).
Interprets to staff the application and implementation of the philosophy, objectives, policies, and procedures of the unit(s), department, and organization; communicates expectations nd monitors staff performance.
Participates in unit goal and program planning, development, and evaluation of programs and special projects as assigned; participates in and supports continuous quality, process, and performance improvement and risk management programs at the unit(s) level.
Provides competent and compassionate patient care (appropriate to age and condition of the patient), serving as a role model and mentor; and assists with unit workload.
Serves as a liaison to the Patient Care Manager.

Qualifications

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Any combination of education and experience that would likely provide the required knowledge, skills and abilities as well as possession of any required licenses or certifications is qualifying.

Education:
Bachelor's Degree in Nursing from an accredited college or university.

Experience:
Two (2) years of progressively responsible and directly related work experience.

License/Certification

Registered Nurse by California Board of Registered Nursing
Basic Life Support by American Heart Association (AHA)
or

Ability to use information and keep abreast of developments in technology to communicate, manage knowledge, mitigate error, and support decision-making in patient care.
Knowledge of current theories, principles, practices, standards, emerging technologies, techniques and approaches in the nursing profession, and the health care system, and the responsibility and accountability for the outcome of practice.
Knowledge of laws, rules and regulations; standards and guidelines of certifying and accrediting bodies; hospital and department/unit standards, protocols, policies and procedures governing the provision of nursing care in the area of assignment.

About Atlas

Atlas is a trusted leader in environmental and infrastructure consulting services; we provide services that enable communities to flourish and thrive. With a team of 3,500 employees and offices throughout the US, we combine local expertise and a network of relationships to deliver solutions to both public and private clients. Our services help improve the quality of life in the communities where we live and work. We always aim for smart, safe, and sustainable results. At Atlas we understand that our future is everyone’s responsibility, and we create a better experience at every stage of a project.

Job Description

Atlas is seeking an experienced Environmental Leader
to drive the growth and operational success of our Bakersfield, CA environmental practice. This leadership role encompasses responsibility for project delivery, client relationship management, team leadership, business development, financial performance, safety, and quality across a broad range of environmental consulting services throughout the Bakersfield and Central Valley markets.

While this is not solely a P&A-focused position, candidates with consulting experience supporting oil and gas plugging and abandonment programs, orphan and idle well remediation, facility decommissioning, methane management, environmental characterization, site restoration, and regulatory closure efforts will be particularly well positioned for success. The successful candidate will serve as a trusted advisor to clients and a leader within the organization, combining strong technical and operational capabilities with a proven ability to develop business, mentor staff, and collaboratively deliver complex environmental projects.

Core Responsibilities

Bakersfield Environmental Team Leadership

Serve as a local environmental lead for the Bakersfield team, helping coordinate staff, project resources, field execution, and operational priorities.
Lead and mentor environmental professionals, project managers, field staff, and subcontracted resources assigned to projects in the Bakersfield/Central Valley area.
Promote a collaborative, accountable team culture focused on safety, responsiveness, technical quality, and client service.
Support workload planning, staff development, project assignments, and coordination with regional and practice leadership.

Project and Program Delivery

Manage environmental projects from pursuit and scoping through execution, reporting, invoicing, and closeout.
Manage scope, schedule, budget, staffing, subcontractor coordination, and profitability for assigned projects.
Coordinate multidisciplinary teams including environmental scientists, engineers, geologists, hydrogeologists, geophysicists, construction/field managers, and outside contractors.
Provide senior-level oversight, risk awareness, and issue resolution for complex field programs and client deliverables.
Ensure compliance with client requirements, regulatory standards, Atlas quality expectations, and Atlas health and safety procedures.

Oil & Gas / P&A Support (Preferred Experience)

Support oil and gas well plugging and abandonment, orphan/idle well remediation, well closure, methane reduction, and oilfield decommissioning projects as applicable.
Coordinate or support well file reviews, site reconnaissance, well/site assessments, methane screening or monitoring, abandonment planning, site restoration, and regulatory closeout documentation.
Work with P&A technical leads and subcontractors to help align field execution with approved work plans, quality expectations, safety requirements, and client objectives.
Support decommissioning of associated oilfield facilities, including tanks, pipelines, surface equipment, waste profiling, soil characterization, and site restoration activities.
Recognize and escalate complex downhole, regulatory, safety, access, stakeholder, cost, or schedule issues to the appropriate technical and regional leaders.

Client, Regulatory, and Stakeholder Coordination

Serve as a client-facing lead for assigned environmental work and maintain strong working relationships with public and private clients, regulators, subcontractors, landowners, and internal stakeholders.
Coordinate communication with agencies, clients, project teams, and subcontractors to support timely decisions, efficient field execution, and clear documentation.
Support stakeholder engagement, site access planning, communications, and documentation for work in urban, industrial, oilfield, or sensitive community settings.
Help prepare project updates, client briefings, meeting materials, technical memoranda, and closeout deliverables.

Business Development and Market Growth

Support growth of environmental services in the Bakersfield/Central Valley market, including existing client expansion and pursuit of new environmental opportunities.
Assist with proposal strategy, scopes of work, fee development, teaming strategies, and client presentations.
Identify opportunities related to environmental investigation and remediation, compliance, oil and gas support, facilities decommissioning, site restoration, and related consulting services.
Collaborate with regional leadership and subject matter experts to position Atlas for public and private sector opportunities.

Quality, Safety, and Financial Accountability

Promote a strong safety culture and ensure field activities are planned and executed consistent with Atlas health and safety expectations.
Monitor project financial performance, including budget status, labor/subcontractor usage, WIP, invoicing, AR support, and change management needs.
Review deliverables for accuracy, consistency, and technical quality appropriate to the role and project scope.
Support continuous improvement in project execution, documentation, subcontractor management, and client service delivery.

You’ll thrive here if you have

Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, geology, engineering, petroleum engineering, or a related field; equivalent experience may be considered.
10+ years of environmental consulting, oil and gas, remediation, construction management, or related project/program delivery experience preferred.
Demonstrated experience leading environmental projects, field teams, subcontractors, budgets, schedules, and client deliverables.
Preferred experience with oil and gas P&A, orphan/idle well programs, wellsite assessment, oilfield facility decommissioning, methane assessment, soil characterization, waste profiling, or site restoration.
Experience working with regulatory agencies and preparing or supporting technical work plans, reports, permits, closeout documents, or compliance documentation.
Strong client service, communication, collaboration, and issue-resolution skills.
Ability to support business development, proposals, client meetings, and strategic growth initiatives.
Professional registration such as P.E. or P.G. is preferred but not required, depending on the candidate’s technical background and role alignment.
Working knowledge of health and safety expectations for environmental field work; OSHA 40-hour HAZWOPER preferred or ability to obtain if required by project assignments.
Ability to travel locally and regionally as needed to support project delivery, client meetings, field oversight, and team coordination.
Hybrid office/field role. Work may include indoor office activities and outdoor field assignments in industrial, construction, oilfield, urban, or remote settings. Field assignments may require walking, standing, bending, climbing, use of PPE, and occasional lifting/carrying in accordance with project-specific health and safety requirements.

What You Can Expect From Us

The A-Team Experience is our employee program focused on helping our people thrive professionally, personally and as part of a community. We trust our people to do great work and live fulfilling lives, and we provide resources that care for our people, both at work and in life:

Health & Wellness: We offer medical, dental and vision coverage with multiple plan options, including no-cost employee-only medical coverage.
Time Off & Family Support: We offer vacation time, paid holidays, sick & safety leave (SSL) and paid parental leave
Retirement: We help employees plan for the future with a 401(k) and company match.
Insurance: To provide protection and peace of mind, we offer Life, AD&D (Accidental Death & Dismemberment) and Disability insurance.
Safety Program: We are committed to safety as part of our ‘quality of life’ core value, and we provide approved PPE at no cost and reimbursement for prescription safety glasses and protective footwear.
Learning & Development: We provide clear career paths, learning resources and development programs allowing you to see how you can grow and advance within the company. We offer internal certifications on specific skills and support external credentials through tuition reimbursement.
Belonging: We support Employee Communities (ECs), voluntary, employee-led groups that create connections, belonging and shared purposes.
Flexibility: May vary by project demands and regional workloads, but we are committed to providing reasonable accommodation to help employees manage their personal and professional responsibilities.

Our people and our culture are central to our work. Our values bring us together, create a sense of belonging and give us purpose. They guide how we make decisions, how we work as a team and how we serve our clients.

Life: We enhance the quality of life. We value people and safety above all else.
Heart: As our hallmark, we act with compassion, empathy, and respect.
Trust: We work together as partners, doing what we say with full accountability.
Mastery: Always striving for the highest quality, greatness inspires our work.

Track record of starting in ambiguity and creating clarity: designing programs, teams, and processes that deliver high-quality outcomes fast.

Passion for customer success and delivering measurable impact for global businesses and experts.

Prepare for and actively participate in case conferences, leading discussions when necessary.
Develop a care plan in collaboration with the member and address social needs with the support of the Community Health Partner.
Conduct regular clinical visits and follow-ups per program guidelines, monitoring routine therapeutic interventions and addressing member needs promptly.
Collaborate with the care team to support a panel of assigned members, providing clinical assistance in health maintenance, chronic disease management, and co-occurring psychiatric disorder support.
Perform medication reconciliation, administration, compliance, and education as part of member care.
Address quality gaps prioritized by the contracted company and ensure thorough chart documentation and coding (ICD or CPT) to validate gap closures.
Utilize care facilitation tools, electronic health records, and scheduling platforms to gather data, document member interactions, organize information, track tasks, and communicate with team members and community resources.
Support members in achieving their care plan goals through coordinated and comprehensive care efforts.

Requirements For The Role

Active, unrestricted Registered Nurse license in the state in which you are seeking employment with Cityblock
You have 3+ years of experience providing clinical services to Adult and/or Geriatric individuals with co-occurring chronic medical and behavioral health conditions
Familiarity and willingness to travel within your community (home-based member visits) and its healthcare systems (hospitals and rehab centers)
Experienced in documentation, care planning, care coordination and have excellent writing skills
Experience and comfort working within an interdisciplinary care team, and specifically working alongside community health workers and care coordination team members
Must have prior experience, and/or willingness to train in clinical nursing skills such as wound assessment and care, blood drawing (venipuncture & phlebotomy), assessment and care plan reinforcement for common chronic conditions such as diabetes, hypertension, CHF, depression.

Education

Graduate of an accredited school of nursing (R.N.)

new_jobs.description:
Case Manager Career Opportunity

Recognized For Your Abilities As a Case Manager

Are you ready for a Case Management role that brings your career closer to home and heart? Join Encompass Health, where being a Case Manager goes beyond just a job; it positions you as a vital link between exceptional care and the transformative impact on each patient's journey. As the leading provider of rehabilitation care in the nation, this opportunity allows you to leverage your clinical expertise while contributing to the well-being of individuals in your community. Manage resources, coordinate patient care from admission to post-discharge, and oversee interdisciplinary plan-of-care decisions. This is more than a career move; it's a chance to shape a future where care and compassion converge for truly meaningful outcomes.

A Glimpse into Our World

At Encompass Health, you'll experience the difference the moment you become a part of our team. Working with us means aligning with a rapidly growing national inpatient rehabilitation leader. We take pride in the growth opportunities we offer and how our team unites for the greater good of our patients. Our achievements include being named one of the "World's Most Admired Companies" and receiving the Fortune 100 Best Companies to Work For® Award, among other accolades, which is nothing short of amazing.

Starting Perks And Benefits

At Encompass Health, we are committed to creating a supportive, inclusive, and caring environment where you can thrive. From day one, you will have access to:

Affordable medical, dental, and vision plans for both full-time and part-time employees and their families.
Generous paid time off that accrues over time.
Opportunities for tuition reimbursement and continuous education.
Company-matching 401(k) and employee stock purchase plans.
Flexible spending and health savings accounts.
A vibrant community of individuals passionate about the work they do!

Become the Case Manager you always wanted to be

Work with interdisciplinary team, guiding treatment plans based on patient needs and preferences.
Coordinate with interdisciplinary team to establish tentative discharge plan and contingency plans.
Participate in planning for and the execution of patient discharge experience.
Monitor patient experience: quality/timeliness/service appropriateness/payors/expectations.
Facilitate team conferences weekly and coordinate all treatment plan modifications.
Complete case management addendums and all required documentation.
Maintain knowledge of regulations/standards, company policies/procedures, and department operations.
Review/analyze case management reports, including Key Care Indicators, and plan appropriate actions.
Understand commercial contract levels, exclusions, payor requirements, and recertification needs.
Attend Acute Care Transfer (ACT) meetings to identify trends and collaboratively reduce ACTs.
Meet with patient/family per Patient Arrival and Initial Visit Standard within 24 hrs of admission.
Perform assessment of goals and complete case management addendum within 48 hours of admission.
Educate patient/family on rehabilitation and Case Manager role; establish communication plan.
Schedule and facilitate family conferences as needed.
Assist patient with timely procuring/planning of resources to avoid discharge delays or issues.
Monitor compliance with regulations for orthotics and prosthetics ordering and payment.
Make appropriate/timely referrals, including documentation to post discharge providers/physicians.
Ensure accuracy of discharge and payor-related information in the patient record.
Participate in utilization review process: data collection, trend review, and resolution actions.
Participate in case management on-call schedule as needed.

Qualifications

License or Certification:
Must be qualified to independently complete an assessment within the scope of practice of his/her discipline (for example, RN, SW, OT, PT, ST, and Rehabilitation Counseling).
If licensure is required for one's discipline within the state, individual must hold an active license.
Must meet eligibility requirements for CCM® or ACM™ certification upon entry into this position OR within two years of entry into the position.
CCM® or ACM™ certification required OR must be obtained within two years of being placed in the Case Manager II position.

Minimum Qualifications:
For Nursing, must possess minimum of an Associate Degree in Nursing, RN licensure with BSN preferred. A diploma is acceptable only in those states whose minimum requirement for licensure or certification is a diploma rather than an Associate Degree.
For all other eligible licensed or certified health care professionals, must possess a minimum of a bachelor's degree and graduate degree is preferred.
2 years of rehabilitation experience preferred.

The Encompass Health Way

We proudly set the standard in care by leading with empathy, doing what's right, focusing on the positive, and standing stronger together. Encompass Health is a trusted leader in post-acute care with over 150 nationwide locations and a team of 36,000 exceptional individuals and growing!

At Encompass Health, we celebrate and welcome diversity in our inclusive culture. We provide equal employment opportunities regardless of race, ethnicity, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, religion, national origin, color, creed, age, mental or physical disability, or any other protected classification.

At MercyOne, health care is more than just a doctor’s visit or a place to go when you’re in need of medical attention. Our Mission is based on improving the health of our communities – that means not only when you are sick but keeping you well.

new_jobs.title: RN Care Coordinator (32 hours, Days)
new_jobs.description:
Job Summary

Inpatient Care Managers are Registered Nurses who independently assure patients are admitted to the correct level of care for accurate billing and reimbursement, provide quality, cost effective clinical coordination/care management in acute care and emergency care settings, manage patients with routine and complex transition planning needs by independently assessing needs, developing, and implementing plans of care for transitions across care settings. Inpatient Care Manager also serve as expert consultants and educators for physicians and other health care team members for discharge and transitional care, coordination of internal and community resources, and support the evaluation and improvement of systems of care to support the optimal utilization of health care resources, while maintaining quality of patient care. The Inpatient Care Manager assumes primary accountability for anticipating, assessing, developing, implementing, documenting, advising, and communicating a safe transition plan of care for patients with complex care needs.

Essential Responsibilities

Coordinates post-discharge patient care needs to assure the timely and effective discharge of routine and complex patients from the hospital setting.
Independently and proactively completes and documents patient assessments which are thorough, timely, age appropriate, and reflect psychosocial support systems, care needs, health plan benefits, level of care determinations for hospitalized patients.
Coordinates and communicates with patients, families, and the health care team to develop mutually agreeable plans of care that optimize the use of resources to support the particular needs of individual patients.
Facilitates resolution of issues which present barriers to safe transfers through the use of patient/team care conferences to assure the efficient transition to a lower level of care and to assure the patient/family receives the right care at the right time so that quality and utilization of resources are simultaneously enhanced.
Ensures systematic and ongoing contact with interdisciplinary staff and continuing care services to assure the safe transition of patients across care settings.
In collaboration with the interdisciplinary health care team, ensures regulatory and compliance standards are met.
Perform duties as requested.

Experience

Basic Qualifications:

Minimum of two years combined RN experience in the following areas:
Med/Surg (hospital acute care)
ICU (hospital acute care)
Emergency Department
Home Health
Skilled Nursing Facilities
Hospice
Long Term Acute Care
Inpatient Rehab
Utilization Management

Education

Successful completion of an RN program by date of hire.
High School Diploma or General Education Development (GED) required.

License, Certification, Registration

This job requires credentials from multiple states. Credentials from the primary work state are required at hire. Additional Credentials from the secondary work state(s) are required post hire.
Registered Nurse License (Washington) within 6 months of hire OR Compact License: Registered Nurse within 6 months of hire
Registered Nurse License (Oregon) within 6 months of hire
Basic Life Support within 3 months of hire

Additional Requirements

Demonstrated ability to interrelate with physicians, nurses, support staff, and patients in interdisciplinary approach.
Demonstrated ability to work as part of a team and work as a constant patient advocate.
Basic physical, psychosocial, functional assessment skills.
Familiar with care process related to discharge and transitional facilities and services.
Thorough knowledge of principles of teaching and delegation, assessment skills and care planning, and appropriate
utilization of acute hospital, long-term care, and home care resources.
Able to develop concise and thorough documentation of patient clinical assessment and care needs.
Highly effective problem solving, written and verbal communication, customer service, organizational and time
management skills.
Ability to effectively provide culturally competent care.
Ability to navigate conflict in high pressure situations.
Ability to use fixed and mobile technological devices.

Preferred Qualifications

Knowledge of appropriate utilization of acute hospital and Kaiser Permanente internal resources.
Knowledge of Medicare and Medicaid regulations related to eligibility requirements: hospital, nursing facilities, home
health, hospice, and Durable Medical Equipment (DME).
Knowledge of utilization management principles and tools.
Demonstrated clinical judgment and customer-focused service skills.
Knowledge of principles of patient teaching, disease prevention measures, and physical assessment as it relates to the
needs of patient and the next level of care.
Certified in Case Management.
BSN or bachelors degree and MSN.

new_jobs.description:
Job Description

The GME Program Coordinator supports the in the management and oversight of one or more fellowship training programs in accordance with the Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME), specialty boards, and subspecialty boards. They must work independently, assisting the Director of GME and the Program Directors in a wide variety of program management and administrative duties, facilitating the evaluation process and preparing and maintaining records for program accreditation. The GME Program Coordinator creates and maintains trainee rotation and departmental education conference schedule and works with fellows by providing guidance and direction for the successful completion of the training program. He or She will work closely with the entire NCH DE Graduate Medical education team, Nemours clinical departments and NCH DE administrative leadership as well as with accrediting agencies to ensure program compliance

Responsibilities

Provides administrative assistance to the administrative staff of the fellowship training program including the Program Director, Associate Program Director, Director of Graduate Medical Education, fellows in training.

Assists with the development and implementation of division, department and institutional procedures and policies as pertinent to department office operations.
Assists in development of policies and procedures in response to various government and regulatory bodies (e.g. RRC, ACGME, , ABP, NRMP, ERAS, AAP, etc.); assists in the development and implementation of and compliance with all policies and procedures relevant to the Residency Program.
Coordinates and/or supports the recruiting for the fellowship training programs and other programs as needed or assigned. Performs initial screening of applicants to the program within existing protocols; manages all listings, updates, and operational aspects of the residency program.
Coordinates all aspects of the trainee application process including responding to inquiries, evaluating applications, reviewing, and verifying credentials, scheduling interviews, generating follow-up correspondence, and maintaining appropriate records.
Assures house staff is appropriately licensed, insured, HIPAA trained, have appropriate immunization status, and comply with background check and drug screening.
Supplies orientation materials to trainees as needed
Serves as gatekeeper for approval for computer access and use of Medical Records. Submit Epic requests for all house staff and coordinates scheduling of appropriate training on hospital systems.
Maintains house staff and faculty scholarly activity
Prepares annual documentation needed for accreditation.
Serves as a member of, develop agendas, take minutes, and implement decision and actions for residency/fellowship committees (i.e., CCC Committees, Program Evaluation Committees (PEC), etc)
Assists in creating rotations schedules and tracking off-site rotations
Serves as an advisor to fellows regarding licensing, Visa Sponsorship, and examinations
Coordinates and facilitates trainee checkout process, exit interviews with program director, and preparation of all final evaluations
Assists finance Department in data collections for GME reimbursement.
Maintains system of review of affiliation agreement and PLAs prior to expiration.

Enters and maintains listing of house staff information using accreditation and hospital GME database (New Innovations)

Verify and process check requests for background check and laboratory vendors
Supports development of fellowship program budget; assembles data for budget development; conducts research for new Program initiatives; investigates costs of new projects and research new funding resources.
Monitors all expenditures for fellowship program; prepares for signature all check requests for travel expenses and education allowances for pediatric house staff.
Support the coordination of special events for the training program, retreats, graduations, banquets, orientation.
Provide back-up to Fellowship/Visiting Student Coordinator as needed.

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree or equivalent years of experience required
American Heart Association BLS required
One or more years relevant experience required

About Us

Nemours Children's Health is an internationally recognized pediatric health system serving more than 1.7 million patient encounters each year. We deliver care across six states through two freestanding children’s hospitals — Nemours Children's Hospital, Delaware and Nemours Children's Hospital, Florida — along with a network of more than 80 primary, urgent, and specialty care practices and more than 40 hospital partnerships.

Backed by the Nemours Foundation and Alfred I. duPont Trust, our $1.7B nonprofit system is dedicated to improving children's health through clinical care, research, education, advocacy, and prevention. Our Whole Child Health approach focuses equally on prevention and treatment, partnering with communities to help every child thrive.

Inclusion and belonging guide our strategy and growth. We are committed to culturally relevant care, reducing health disparities, and fostering an environment where every associate, patient, and family feels supported and valued.

new_jobs.title: Program Coordinator (ACP)
new_jobs.description:
Job Summary

This position is located in the Office of Victim Services and Justice Grants (OVSJG), Victim Services Division. The mission of the Office of Victim Services and Justice Grants is to develop, fund, and coordinate programs that improve public safety; enhance the administration of justice; and create systems of care for crime victims, youth, and their families in the District. OVSJG supports and coordinates the development and implementation of a comprehensive system of care for crime victims within the District of Columbia. OVSJG advocates on behalf of victims at all levels of government and community; and works to ensure that comprehensive services are available in the District for victims of crime. The ACP program allows eligible individuals to receive mail at a confidential address and provide a legal substitute address for the individual's physical address on public records. The incumbent is responsible for administering the District's Address Confidentiality Program (ACP), which involves planning, research, data collection, analysis and evaluation, and providing training to community members and advocates.

Duties And Responsibilities

Supports the coordination of the Address Confidentiality Program (ACP) activities in order to develop program policies, procedures, forms, and other materials. Identifies and collects performance metrics for OVSJG to report on the ACP in order to evaluate and address concerns regarding the efficiency and operation of the program. Reviews and provide recommendations on ACP applications to the Program Manager and agency leadership in order to streamline participant enrollment into the program. Interprets and provides guidance to leadership and advocates; advises on unclear or vague policies and procedures relating to the ACP. Identifies problems and specific issues in a particular area of ACP and advises the supervisor of existing problems in order to recommend solutions or alternatives for program implementation and supporting survivors. Develops and provides training to community-based organizations that serve as ACP application assistants for clients in order to aid in their enrollment into the program. Provides guidance and technical assistance to District agencies in order to implement the statutory requirements of the program.

Maintains records of any certified or registered mail received on behalf of a participant. Maintains information and documentation regarding the ACP databases to track actions and provide periodic reporting, or projects that relate to the program. Receives first-class, certified, and registered mail sent to a participant at a substitute address in order to forward mail to respective participants. Represents the program at community events; meets with individuals, community-based organizations, DC government agencies, etc.; participates in related conferences, meetings, and training seminars in order to report findings and essential information back to senior staff. Coordinates project phases with technical and professional stakeholders involved in the project. Provides information, as required by project specifications in order to communicate information and decisions concerning projects with all interested parties.

Qualifications And Education

This position requires at least one (1) year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level in the normal line of progression. Specialized experience is experience which is directly related to the position and has equipped the individual with the knowledge, skills, and abilities to successfully perform the duties of the position.

Licenses and Certifications

None.

Working Conditions/Environment

The work is primarily performed in offices.

new_jobs.title: Student Information Systems & Data Coordinator
new_jobs.description:
The mission of the School District of Waukesha is to develop in our students the capacity
and skills to be community, college and career ready.

Job Summary

Lead the Student Information System at the center of a Large School District.
The School District of Waukesha is seeking an experienced Student Information Systems
& Data Coordinator to serve as the district's functional leader and primary administrator
for Infinite Campus and student information operations.

This position sits at the intersection of technology, school operations, student services,
enrollment, teaching and learning, state reporting, and data.

Infinite Campus is one of the most important enterprise systems in our district. The
information maintained within it affects students, families, teachers, schools, state
reporting, scheduling, communications, assessment, accountability, and dozens of
connected applications.

We are looking for someone who understands that environment and wants the opportunity
to lead it.

Our mission centers around preparing students for community, college, and career. In
this role, accurate data and well-designed systems become part of accomplishing that
mission.

Duties and Responsibilities

Infinite Campus System Leadership
● Serve as the district's primary functional administrator and system owner for Infinite
Campus.
● Maintain district-level configuration, calendars, schools, programs, grading
structures, enrollment structures, user groups, and permissions.
● Coordinate annual school-year setup, rollover, and other major recurring SIS
processes.
● Evaluate new Infinite Campus functionality and coordinate appropriate
implementation.
● Coordinate testing and implementation of major configuration changes.
● Serve as the primary district liaison with Infinite Campus for functional system
support.

WISEdata & State Reporting

● Serve as a primary district leader for WISEdata student reporting.
● Monitor the submission and validation of state-reported data.
● Coordinate resolution of WISEdata errors and data-quality concerns.
● Lead preparation for state snapshots, pupil counts, and other student-data reporting
requirements.
● Collaborate with Enrollment, Student Services, Special Education, multilingual
learner staff, Teaching & Learning, and school personnel to ensure accurate state
reporting.
● Maintain awareness of DPI requirements and changes affecting student information.
Student Data Governance
● Establish and maintain district standards for student-data entry and management.
● Ensure district student-information practices support reliable reporting and
downstream system use.
● Identify systemic data-quality concerns and coordinate corrective processes.
● Help determine the appropriate source of truth and business rules for student
information.
● Partner with district leaders when operational practices require changes to SIS
configuration or data-entry procedures.
Annual SIS Operations
● Coordinate annual calendar and school-year creation.
● Oversee student rollover and future-year setup.
● Support scheduling and enrollment processes from the district SIS perspective.
● Coordinate summer school configuration and related annual processes.
● Maintain a calendar of major SIS activities, reporting deadlines, and recurring
responsibilities.
Student Data Team Leadership
● Provide direction and priorities to the Student Data Quality & Operations Specialist.
● Establish repeatable operational procedures for student-data work.
● Develop appropriate cross-training so critical Infinite Campus functions can continue
during staff absences.
● Support professional learning for school secretaries, registrars, and other Infinite
Campus users.
● Build documentation that reduces reliance on individual institutional knowledge.
Cross-Department Collaboration
● Work closely with school administrators, enrollment personnel, secretaries,
counselors, Student Services, Teaching & Learning, Business Services, and
Technology staff.
● Translate operational needs into appropriate Infinite Campus configuration and
processes.
● Help district departments understand how changes to student information affect
connected systems.
● Serve as a trusted resource when complex student-data questions arise.

Partnership with the Technology Data & Applications Team

This position is part of a deliberately structured Data & Applications team. You will not be
expected to personally own every technical system connected to Infinite Campus. You will
work alongside:
● a Student Data Quality & Operations Specialist focused on data cleanup,
enrollment operations, reconciliation, documentation, and operational SIS support;
● a Technology Assessment Specialist focused on assessment systems, data,
dashboards, and assessment-related processes; and
The SIS Coordinator defines and owns the student-information business rules. The
Integration Engineer builds and maintains the technical plumbing that moves the data. That
separation is intentional.
QUALIFICATIONS
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each duty
satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill,
and/or ability required at the time of hire or for the continuation of employment.
EDUCATION AND/OR EXPERIENCE:
● Bachelor’s Degree and/or equivalent experience is desired.
● We are particularly interested in candidates with meaningful Infinite Campus
experience who understand how a student information system functions within the
real operational environment of a school district.

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:

A successful candidate will demonstrate:
● Experience administering or deeply supporting Infinite Campus or a comparable K-12
student information system.
● Strong understanding of student enrollment, scheduling, calendars, grading,
programs, and school-year processes.
● Understanding of data quality and the importance of accurate source-system
information.
● Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
● Ability to organize complicated annual and recurring processes.
● Ability to communicate effectively with technical staff, administrators, school
secretaries, teachers, and other stakeholders.
● Ability to establish standards while remaining responsive to school and department
needs.
● Strong documentation and training skills.
● Ability to manage multiple priorities without losing sight of long-term system health.
● A collaborative approach to solving organizational problems.
● Strong interpersonal skills with ability to empathize and find common ground for the
good of the organization.
● Ability to work as a successful team member with co-workers.
● Should have a history of confidentiality, stability, neatness, punctuality, loyalty,
ethical consciousness, organizational skills, and flexibility.

Experience with Wisconsin WISEdata reporting, DPI systems, Ed-Fi, or Wisconsin
school-district student-data processes is highly desirable.

new_jobs.title: Grantmaking Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
About The Job

Grantmaking Program Manager

Title: Grantmaking Program Manager

Job code: 8223GG

Employee Group: Civil Service (exempt) Full/Part Time (FTE): Full Time (100% FTE)

Regular/Temporary: Regular

About The Job

The University of Minnesota’s Institute on the Environment (IonE) is seeking a Grantmaking Program Manager to lead the planning, implementation, and continuous improvement of the Institute’s grantmaking portfolio. This position manages the full lifecycle of IonE’s competitive funding programs – including Impact Goals Grants , Mini Grants , and other strategic funding opportunities – from program design and Requests for Proposals (RFPs) through application review, award administration, stewardship, reporting, evaluation, and closeout.

Working collaboratively across IonE’s leadership, research, communications, finance, and administrative teams, the Grantmaking Program Manager serves as the central operational lead for IonE’s grantmaking portfolio – coordinating complex funding cycles, supporting applicants, reviewers, coaches, and funded project teams, and maintaining the authoritative record of the funded portfolio. This position also advances IonE’s strategic commitment to outcomes and impact by developing the metrics, analysis, and reporting that demonstrate portfolio results and inform future funding decisions. Professionals with experience as Program Officers, Program Representatives, Grants Managers, or similar grantmaking roles in foundation, nonprofit, or government funding organizations will find many familiar elements in this position.

The Ideal Candidate

The ideal candidate is an organized project manager, analytical thinker, and relationship builder who enjoys running complex processes exceptionally well while continually looking for ways to improve them. They are naturally curious about the people, ideas, and projects that make up the portfolio and are energized by identifying opportunities to strengthen programs, enhance participant experiences, and increase organizational impact.

They balance strategic thinking with operational excellence - keeping one eye on the long-term evolution of IonE’s grantmaking portfolio while ensuring the day-to-day work is executed with consistency, accuracy, and efficiency. Comfortable navigating both ambiguity and detail, they embrace continuous learning, seek out opportunities for innovation, and build scalable systems that support the portfolio as it evolves. As IonE’s grantmaking portfolio expands in scope and complexity through future funding opportunities and institutional priorities, this position offers meaningful opportunities for the successful candidate to assume broader strategic leadership and organizational impact.

Informational Job Webinar

Register to attend an informational webinar hosted by the supervisor for this position, Director of Administration & Operations April Deinken . We'll share more about the role, what it's like to work at IonE, and answer questions submitted by prospective applicants through the Zoom registration form.

Attendance is completely optional and does not factor into consideration of your application. The webinar is simply an opportunity to learn more about the position and IonE, and to help you determine whether the role feels like a good mutual fit.

When: Wednesday, Sept. 9, 4:00 - 4:45 p.m. CST
Where: Zoom, webinar format
Link to Register

Salary

The salary range for this position is $74k - $86k/yr ($35.65/hr - $41.53/hr). IonE uses a structured compensation approach that considers a position’s salary range as well as a candidate’s relevant experience, skills, and demonstrated proficiency when determining starting salary.

This hiring range reflects an entry-to-intermediate proficiency level for the position. Candidates entering the role may still be developing some position-specific knowledge and skills, while candidates placed toward the higher end of the hiring range would be expected to demonstrate greater proficiency and independence in the core competencies of the position. Employees may progress through the position’s broader salary range over time as they develop greater proficiency and independence, with salary increases considered through the University’s annual merit process and compensation processes.

Work Schedule & Authorization

Work hours are standard office hours, M–F. IonE and the Research and Innovation Office endorse a work with flexibility approach that offers a welcoming and flexible work environment where everyone is inspired to do their best.

This position has been designated as eligible for flexible work profile 2: Profile 2 is expected to work in the office at least 3 days per week (Mon, Wed, Thu), and typically working remotely 1-2 days per week (Tue, Fri). Your office location will be located at 1954 Buford Ave, Saint Paul, MN 55108. IonE management retains the right to modify flexible work arrangement agreements on a temporary or permanent basis for any reason at any time.

The candidate must reside locally; IonE can potentially provide up to $1,500 of relocation assistance for the ideal candidate. If you currently reside out-of-state and are willing to relocate to the Mpls-St.Paul area, please indicate as much in your cover letter.

Applicants must currently be authorized to work in the United States. IonE is unable to provide employment-based visa sponsorship for this position.

Responsibilities

Grantmaking Program Management (50%)

Run the funding cycles: Lead IonE’s competitive funding programs from program design through award notification, maintaining the systems that keep those cycles consistent and repeatable.

Develop and manage the annual grantmaking calendar, establishing timelines, priorities, and dependencies across IonE’s funding portfolio
Develop and refine RFPs, application materials, review criteria, award documentation, Terms & Conditions, and reporting requirements
Coordinate application and review processes, including recruiting and orienting reviewers, matching reviewers to proposals based on expertise and conflicts of interest, developing award recommendations, and award notifications
Develop resources, guidance, tools, and training materials that enable applicants, reviewers, and coaches to participate successfully throughout the funding lifecycle
Develop and maintain the workflows, templates, standard operating procedures, and records that promote consistency and continuity across grantmaking programs
Collaborate with leadership, research, communications, finance, and administrative staff to align funding cycles with IonE priorities and operational capacity
Continuously assess grantmaking processes and participant experiences, identifying opportunities to improve funding models, eligibility criteria, policies, and practices that strengthen the effectiveness, accessibility, equity, and overall participant experience of IonE’s grantmaking programs

Award Stewardship & Portfolio Records (30%)

Steward funded projects: Serve as the primary relationship holder for funded teams and keep the record of the portfolio accurate and current.

Serve as the primary point of contact for applicants, reviewers, coaches, and funded project teams throughout the funding lifecycle Coordinate award setup, reporting schedules, amendments, no-cost extensions, rebudget requests, and project closeout
Monitor project progress, budgets, expenditures, and compliance with award requirements, proactively engaging with project teams to support timely reporting and milestone completion
Maintain the authoritative record of funded projects, including updating IonE’s public-facing project directory throughout the lifecycle, in accordance with web content standards
Partner with IonE’s public interest communications team by providing regular updates on project milestones, findings, and other storytelling opportunities, and by flagging project directory changes that affect editorial content
Coordinate the collection of project outputs, photos, testimonials, and other assets that support impact reporting and storytelling
Coordinate grant coaching meetings, workshops, and other stewardship activities that support funded teams

Portfolio Evaluation & Reporting (20%)

Measure and communicate impact: Develop the metrics and analyses that show what the portfolio produces and inform what it funds next.

Develop and refine portfolio-wide metrics, evaluation frameworks, and reporting processing aligned with IonE’s strategic priorities
Analyze qualitative and quantitative portfolio data to identify trends, outcomes, and opportunities for continuous improvement
Produce reports and portfolio analyses that inform leadership decisions and provide evidence of the Institute’s impact to internal and external audiences
Assess portfolio performance and outcomes to identify opportunities for continuous improvement and inform future funding priorities and program design
Identify emerging themes and success stories across the grant portfolio to inform strategic planning and communications

General Responsibilities

Like all IonE staff, the Grantmaking Program Manager participates in IonE-wide initiatives, staff meetings, events, and professional development activities; contributes to a collaborative, inclusive, and service-oriented organizational culture; and performs other duties as assigned.

Strong candidates will demonstrate...

A track record of running deadline-driven processes from start to finish: cycles, cohorts, or campaigns that shipped on time, repeatedly
A commitment to follow-through on the unglamorous middle: chasing late reports, closing loops, keeping records current without being asked
The ability to serve as the primary point of contact for a complex portfolio while remaining responsive, organized, and composed across multiple stakeholders and competing priorities
A strong service orientation toward the people inside of a process; ensuring applicants, reviewers, and grantees experience interactions as helpful, clear, and fair
A habit of documenting work and improving systems as they go, leaving processes stronger and more sustainable over time
Fluency moving between operational detail and strategic perspective, recognizing patterns in portfolio data and communicating insights clearly to diverse audiences
Sound judgment about when to resolve issues independently, when to seek input, and when to escalate concerns
Curiosity and a continuous improvement mindset, with a proactive approach to building relationships and developing a deep understanding of the people, projects, and outcomes across the portfolio to effectively represent the work and identify opportunities to strengthen programs over time.

Qualifications

Required Qualifications

BA/BS degree plus at least four years of relevant professional experience, or a combination of related education and work experience totaling eight years
Experience managing multi-phase programs, funding cycles, or similarly complex processes involving hard deadlines and multiple stakeholders
Experience administering grants, awards, contracts, or other funded agreements from either the grantmaking or grant-seeking perspective
Demonstrated ability to build and maintain organized records, workflows, documentation, and operational systems
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience producing clear guidance or reports for varied audiences
Proficiency with common productivity and data tools (e.g., Google Workspace, Excel/Sheets) and the ability to learn new platforms quickly

Preferred Qualifications

Experience in a university, research, philanthropic, or nonprofit funding environment
Experience designing or improving requests for proposals (RFPs), review processes, or reporting requirements
Experience with survey and data-collection tools (e.g., Qualtrics) and analyzing qualitative and quantitative program data
Experience developing metrics, basic data analysis, dashboards, or evaluation

new_jobs.title: Environmental Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
About Atlas

Atlas is a trusted leader in environmental and infrastructure consulting services; we provide services that enable communities to flourish and thrive. With a team of 3,500 employees and offices throughout the US, we combine local expertise and a network of relationships to deliver solutions to both public and private clients. Our services help improve the quality of life in the communities where we live and work. We always aim for smart, safe, and sustainable results. At Atlas we understand that our future is everyone’s responsibility, and we create a better experience at every stage of a project.

Job Description

Atlas is seeking an Environmental Program Manager
to lead environmental investigation, remediation, and Brownfields projects across Ohio, Kentucky, and Indiana. In this role, you will manage complex projects from proposal through completion while supporting business growth, mentoring technical staff, and helping clients navigate environmental challenges safely and effectively.

This position is based in Sharonville, Ohio
, and plays a key role in delivering projects that support environmental stewardship and community revitalization.

Core Responsibilities

Manage day-to-day operations for due diligence, subsurface investigation, remediation, and Brownfields projects throughout Ohio as well as Kentucky and Indiana, including all aspects of the project life cycle such as proposal generation, technical execution, reporting, and invoicing.
Provide strong technical leadership and mentorship for the Cincinnati team.
Manage projects that are large and complex in scope with multiple subcontractors and internal team members.
Identify and pursue new business opportunities and partnerships with clients and regulators to drive growth and expansion of the business.
Actively participate in professional and technical organizations appropriate for core skill set and client needs.
Provide senior review for reports by assisting with data interpretation, evaluation, and comparison to state and/or federal environmental regulatory standards.
Professionally interact with internal and external clients, service partners, and contractors.
Collaborate with other team members toward a common goal of providing client-centric services with high-quality interactions and deliverables.
Set a common vision and enable technical team members to be successful.
Identify and set goals for team members' contributions to a project.
Communicate with and align team behind scope of work to maximize outcomes for all stakeholders.
Manage health and safety to achieve zero incidents.
Provide assistance with proposal efforts, including technical approach, level of effort, and staffing requirements.
Assure timely and accurate submittal of invoices. Monitor and report the status of accounts receivable and recommend appropriate action on overdue accounts.
Embrace and model the Atlas core values including Trust, Mastery, Heart, and Life.

You’ll thrive here if you have

Bachelor’s or Master's degree in Environmental Science, Soil Science, Geology, Engineering, or other applied science,
At least 10 years experience with project management, staff management, field work, data evaluation, technical writing, and QA/QC in the environmental consulting field,
Subject matter expert for procedures and methodologies related to due diligence, site investigation, remediation, and/or environmental compliance,
Experience with client management, business development, and participation in local professional organizations,
Experience with implementation and supervision of health and safety requirements,
Proficiency in MS Office (Word, Outlook, Teams, Excel, and PowerPoint),
Excellent time management skills, attention to detail, and ability to manage multiple activities on an ongoing basis.
Excellent oral and written communication skills,
Demonstrated ability to lead project teams with projects of advanced technical scope and complexity,
Ability to manage scope, schedule, and budget to maintain profitability of projects, and Experience with complex remediation projects
OSHA 40-hr HAZWOPER certification, with current 8-hr annual refreshers
Familiar with SharePoint, MS Excel/Word, and PDF documents
Experience with environmental consulting and project management in Ohio, Indiana, and Kentucky

What You Can Expect From Us

The A-Team Experience is our employee program focused on helping our people thrive professionally, personally and as part of a community. We trust our people to do great work and live fulfilling lives, and we provide resources that care for our people, both at work and in life:

Health & Wellness: We offer medical, dental and vision coverage with multiple plan options, including no-cost employee-only medical coverage.
Time Off & Family Support: We offer vacation time, paid holidays, sick & safety leave (SSL) and paid parental leave
Retirement: We help employees plan for the future with a 401(k) and company match.
Insurance: To provide protection and peace of mind, we offer Life, AD&D (Accidental Death & Dismemberment) and Disability insurance.
Safety Program: We are committed to safety as part of our ‘quality of life’ core value, and we provide approved PPE at no cost and reimbursement for prescription safety glasses and protective footwear.
Learning & Development: We provide clear career paths, learning resources and development programs allowing you to see how you can grow and advance within the company. We offer internal certifications on specific skills and support external credentials through tuition reimbursement.
Belonging: We support Employee Communities (ECs), voluntary, employee-led groups that create connections, belonging and shared purposes.
Flexibility: May vary by project demands and regional workloads, but we are committed to providing reasonable accommodation to help employees manage their personal and professional responsibilities.

Our people and our culture are central to our work. Our values bring us together, create a sense of belonging and give us purpose. They guide how we make decisions, how we work as a team and how we serve our clients.

Life: We enhance the quality of life. We value people and safety above all else.
Heart: As our hallmark, we act with compassion, empathy, and respect.
Trust: We work together as partners, doing what we say with full accountability.
Mastery: Always striving for the highest quality, greatness inspires our work.

About The Job

Career Level: Management

The overall purpose of this position is to achieve IEEE's goal to have the greatest impact possible on inspiring students in engineering and technology, from basic awareness to academic success to preparing them for professional practice. The role will provide leadership in supporting the implementation and delivery of pre-university and university education resources designed for students and educators. This might include recommending improvements, day to day program execution, and developing new programs to improve IEEE's educational resources.

A primary responsibility for this position is overseeing the daily operations of the Engineering Projects in Community Service (EPICS) in IEEE program. This includes advancing EPICS as a flagship program for IEEE that supports service learning and empowers student members to develop sustainable technical solutions that impact communities around the world. The Specialist is expected to develop a deep knowledge of EPICS in IEEE operations and an understanding of the mission and goals to ensure they align with and meet IEEE's strategic objectives.

The Specialist will work with EPICS in IEEE volunteer leaders and collaborate closely with volunteers and staff within Educational Activities as well as all appropriate areas of IEEE in order to maintain and enhance EPICS operations. The Specialist will have primary responsibility for developing educational resources, managing the annual budget, maintaining records, compiling and preparing reports, collaborating and communicating with staff and Section leadership to process payments, overseeing the awarding and implementation of projects and ensuring compliance with IEEE methods and procedures.

An important function of this role, is collaboration with key volunteer leaders and staff, is the development, execution, and evaluation of strategies to ensure that EPICS in IEEE is a sustainable and growing program that impacts the technical, professional, and humanitarian aspirations of IEEE student members. The Specialist reports to the Sr. Manager, University Programs and Partnerships. This position works under general guidelines on overall business strategies and objectives; and is authorized to approve program expenditures within limits determined by the Educational Activities Department.

Key Responsibilities

Program Management - 50%

Directs the planning, strategic implementation and delivery of the overall EPICS in IEEE program and its activities in accordance with the mission and the goals of IEEE EAB (Educational Activities Board)
Identifies and develops new opportunities and partnerships to support the strategic direction of the program
Develops and implements communications and systems to ensure funds are distributed and reports are maintained
Designs and administers the processes and systems needed for the submission, screening, committee evaluation, and funding recommendations for the identification and selection of project proposals

Supports the work of the EPICS in IEEE Committee and collaborates with other EA and IEEE committees, volunteers and staff as needed
